title: Fix non-working Home 'Order Now' and restore TREY-C security functionality

requirements.text: Fix the Home (Landing) page CTA buttons (including the "Order Now" button) so they reliably navigate to the intended routes and never appear unclickable due to layout/overlay issues.

quotes: Fix the home screen order now buttons and any others buttons not working some are not working

acceptanceCriteria: On the Home (/) page, clicking "Order Now" triggers a route change (no dead click).
On the Home (/) page, clicking "Get Started" triggers a route change (no dead click).
On the Home (/) page, clicking "Learn More" triggers a route change (no dead click).
Buttons are not blocked by any full-screen/absolute-positioned layers (no element overlays capturing pointer events).
No console errors are emitted when clicking the buttons (in a production build).

requirements.text: Audit and fix any other non-working buttons/CTAs across the app by ensuring each interactive element has a valid handler (navigate, submit, mutation) and is not accidentally disabled or blocked by an overlay; prioritize primary conversion/navigation buttons in the header and marketing pages.

quotes: and any others buttons not working some are not working

acceptanceCriteria: All primary navigation actions in the header (BrandHeader) are clickable and navigate correctly on both desktop and mobile (including the mobile menu buttons).
No button that appears enabled is a no-op (every visible CTA performs its expected action).
If a button must be disabled due to auth/state, the UI clearly indicates disabled state and provides an English explanation (e.g., tooltip, inline text, or toast).

requirements.text: Restore and implement "TREY-C security" as a working feature: add backend security state + APIs for enabling/disabling protection, rate limiting configuration, capturing security events, and exposing security stats/events to admins.

quotes: make sure TREY-C security is running again

acceptanceCriteria: Backend exposes callable methods for: (1) reading security config, (2) updating/toggling security config (admin-only), (3) retrieving security stats (admin-only), and (4) retrieving recent security events (admin-only).
When security is enabled, calls are evaluated against the configured rate limit window / max calls per window and produce security events with result = allowed/denied/throttled.
Security events and counters update deterministically based on calls (allowed/denied/throttled counts are consistent with emitted events).
Non-admin callers cannot access admin-only security endpoints (backend traps or returns an appropriate error).

requirements.text: Replace the current placeholder/unavailable TREY-C security UI in the Admin panel with a functional dashboard that reads real security config/stats/events from the backend and allows admins to manage security settings.

quotes: make sure TREY-C security is running again

acceptanceCriteria: The admin "Security Dashboard" section renders real data (not hardcoded stub values) when the backend is available.
Admins can toggle security enabled/disabled from the UI and see the updated state reflected after the mutation completes.
Admins can view security stats (allowed/denied/throttled counts) and a list of recent security events.
If the backend does not support security (e.g., older deployment), the UI shows a clear English error state and does not crash or spin forever.

requirements.text: Implement and display a working TREY-C security protection modal/banner component (currently empty) in a way that does not interfere with clicking underlying buttons/links.

quotes: make sure TREY-C security is running again

acceptanceCriteria: A TREY-C security modal/banner renders with English text indicating protection status.
The modal/banner can be dismissed via an explicit control and does not trap the user on the page.
While visible, the modal does not block critical CTAs unless it is intentionally modal; if it is modal, it must provide an obvious close/dismiss action and restore clickability after dismissal.
After dismissal, the Home page buttons remain clickable and functional.

constraints: Do not edit any files under the frontend immutable paths: frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts, frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.tsx, frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts, frontend/src/main.tsx, frontend/src/components/ui.
Backend must remain a single Motoko actor with all logic in backend/main.mo.
Only create/update backend/migration.mo if new stable/persisted state is introduced or existing stable state shape changes (conditional migration policy).
Use English for all user-facing UI text.
nonGoals: Do not add third-party auth providers (only Internet Identity is allowed).
Do not add external databases or off-chain storage systems.
Do not implement real-time features (no WebSockets/push notifications).
Do not change branding/copy beyond what is required to fix broken buttons and restore the TREY-C security UI.
